sources.name: OpenAPI React Query Codegen security advisory

facts.statement: Ten malicious versions of @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen were published to npm on 2026-08-28 between 20:00 and 20:21 UTC
an attacker who abused a misconfigured GitHub Actions release workflow.
0.5.4 , 1.6.3 , 2.2.1 , 3.0.3 have no install script at all and execute via binding.gyp alone.
latest dist-tag pointed at the malicious 3.0.4
The release workflow was triggered by issue_comment with no author-association gate
No version published before 2026-08-28 is affected.
issue_comment trigger removed; releases run on tag push only
All ten versions deprecated; removal requested from npm security.
The two 0.0.0-* prereleases carry a malicious preinstall but not the payload files

editorial.title: OpenAPI codegen's comment-triggered release shipped malicious npm versions
editorial.summary: The maintainer says an unguarded pull-request comment started a release workflow that published ten malicious @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen versions. Eight numbered versions included payload files; two prereleases had install hooks pointing to missing files. The latest tag briefly pointed to a malicious version.
editorial.why_it_matters: A public comment crossed into a job with publishing rights. Consumers need exact version checks, while maintainers need to review who can start release jobs.
editorial.action: Compare lockfiles and install logs with the advisory's version list. Investigate hosts that installed affected versions and rotate exposed credentials from a clean environment. Audit comment-triggered release jobs with publishing rights.
